headline: Listening Gap Fill Activity - Live Missing-Word Practice
outcomes: Students practise listening for exact words, not only general meaning
The live accuracy breakdown shows which words the class heard clearly and which need another pass
Vocabulary and listening practice connect because the missing words come from the lesson topic
Teachers get a fast, focused listening check without preparing a worksheet
howItWorks: LessonCaptain generates five or six sentences with a missing target word in each one
Students listen, read the sentence context, and type the missing word from their own device
The teacher reveals answers one by one with a live class accuracy breakdown
The class reviews tricky words, spelling, pronunciation, and meaning before moving into speaking practice
teacherUseCases: After a video or listening text, check whether students caught the key vocabulary
Before a speaking task, reinforce pronunciation and spelling of target words
Use as a short accuracy break in a longer conversation lesson

faq.q: Does Listening Gap Fill require an audio file?
faq.a: It can work as a teacher-led listening check using generated sentences, and it fits naturally after source-based lessons where students have just heard or read target language.

faq.q: Is this just a worksheet on screen?
faq.a: No. Students answer live, the teacher sees class accuracy instantly, and the reveal becomes a focused review moment rather than a static fill-in-the-blank page.
Yes. Beginner rounds use short sentences and familiar words. Higher levels can handle more natural phrasing, distractors, and words that are harder to hear.

faq.q: What does the teacher do with wrong answers?
faq.a: Use them diagnostically. If many students miss the same word, replay or reread the sentence, isolate the sound, then ask students to use the word in a new sentence.

faq.q: How do students type their missing-word answers?
faq.a: No. Students type answers through the live browser link without creating accounts or installing anything.
